heroHeadline: UN Names Three New World Restoration Flagships as UNCCD COP17 Closes Without Drought Protocol
heroSubtitle: UNEP and FAO awarded three new UN World Restoration Flagships on August 26 — Brazil's Araticum Cerrado initiative, Saudi Arabia's National Greening Programme, and the 5-country Sahel Integrated Resilience Initiative — bringing the network to 27 recognized restoration projects globally. The Sahel initiative, spanning Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania, and Niger, has rehabilitated 335,000+ ha since 2018 toward a 470,000 ha 2030 target. But the diplomatic backdrop was rockier: UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia (Aug 17–28) closed without a binding global drought protocol after the African Group staged a walkout over US opposition to any international drought instrument, postponing talks to COP18 in Egypt.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNEP, FAO, UNCCD, IUCN, WRI Global Forest Watch, INPE, CBD, NASA, and Tier 2 science outlets. Pledge figures reflect commitments; verified restoration is substantially lower.
